evidence.scope: Full fixed comparison set (Quidra, Python, C++, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift, Zig). Gates are global booleans per methodology; evaluated symmetrically for all 10 languages, not per-language.
evidence.nature_of_available_inputs: These are Quidra core-repository/product documentation files (release workflow, package manager, AI issue triage, and the Quidra 0.1 language specification: architecture, diagnostics, grammar, language semantics, LLM guide, numeric/bin rules, patch schema). They describe the Quidra language and repository, not the llm_learnability evaluation's Learnability Reference Packs, fixtures, transformers, seeds, validators, or audit manifests for any of the 10 languages, including Quidra.
artifacts_required_by_methodology_but_no: Per-language Learnability Reference Packs (one per language, comparable token budget) for the fixed comparison set.
Worked-example fixtures and scored-task fixtures used to build/verify each pack.
Forward/inverse transformers, transformation manifests, deterministic seeds, and round-trip test results (Section 10.4 items 1-5) for I1/I2/I3 keyword/vocabulary/structural transformation conditions.
Positive compile/run fixtures and negative fixtures per condition (Section 10.4 items 6-7), with actual toolchain compile/run output proving each fixture builds and matches expected output.
Harness-convention documentation showing which facts (e.g. file naming, entry-point naming) are supplied by the harness rather than demanded of the model.
Validator pass/fail exercise records (a correct input that passes and a corrupted input that fails) for every validator, including permutation-mapping conditions.
The normalized-token overlap / leakage detector implementation and its output for every worked-example-slot x scored-task pair.
A planted-leak positive control case and proof that the leakage predicate detects it.
Positive reference fixture and deliberately mutated negative fixture stored beside every structural/compliance predicate, with a record that the negative fixture fails for the intended reason.
The audit manifest per scored pack recording pack hash, fixture hash, leakage checks performed, and pass/fail status.
Any evidence that scored requests have not yet been sent (required precondition: no scored trial may begin until every pack passes the leakage audit).

gate.infrastructure_preflight.requirement_summary: Section 10.4 'Mandatory pre-flight validation' requires, before any Reference Pack is built and before any trial is scored, that (1) every fixture compiles/runs on the real toolchain with output matching exactly, (2) every unstated harness convention is satisfied by the harness rather than the model, and (3) every validator can both pass a correct input and fail a corrupted input -- all preserved as evidence.
gate.infrastructure_preflight.finding: No fixtures, harness-convention records, validator pass/fail exercise logs, or toolchain compile/run transcripts for any of the 10 languages were present in this task packet's embedded/readable inputs. The only readable path assigned to this worker (/quidra-benchmark/repo/docs) contains general Quidra product/language documentation and no llm_learnability infrastructure artifacts at all -- for Quidra or for any of the 9 comparison languages.
gate.infrastructure_preflight.reason_this_is_a_blocker_not_a_fabricate: Per worker rule 3 and Section 10.4's own warning that an infrastructure defect in this track 'does not announce itself,' a gate must not be marked true without direct evidence of the required checks having been performed and passed. No such evidence was accessible to this worker. Recording false with this evidence trail is the correct negative-gate result rather than a validator failure.

gate.reference_pack_leakage.requirement_summary: Section 10.4 'Mandatory Reference Pack leakage audit' requires, after pre-flight passes but before any scored model request, a mechanical + blinded-manual audit of every pack (per language, condition, seed, transformation set) against the enumerated leakage predicates, each predicate proven against a planted-leak positive control, plus positive/negative fixtures for every structural predicate, all captured in a per-pack audit manifest (pack hash, fixture hash, checks performed, pass/fail).
gate.reference_pack_leakage.finding: No Learnability Reference Packs, no leakage-detector implementation or output, no planted-leak positive-control test result, and no audit manifest were present in or reachable from this task packet for Quidra or any comparison language. The pre-flight gate above is itself unverified, and Section 10.4 makes the leakage audit strictly dependent on pre-flight already having passed, so this gate cannot be certified independently of that dependency either.
gate.reference_pack_leakage.status: NOT VERIFIED -- infrastructure blocker, and blocked on gate.infrastructure_preflight
gate.reference_pack_leakage.reason_this_is_a_blocker_not_a_fabricate: Absent the manifest, hashes, and planted-control detection evidence the methodology requires to be 'preserved,' asserting pass would be fabricating a value forbidden by worker rule 3. A genuine unmet precondition is recorded as false rather than as N/A, per Section 6/10 guidance that unfinished applicable work is never N/A.

evidence.symmetry_statement: Both gates were evaluated identically across the full fixed 10-language comparison set using the same absence-of-evidence standard; no language received a more lenient or stricter infrastructure-evidence bar than another.
evidence.recommended_remediation: A follow-on work unit needs read access to the actual llm_learnability reference-pack build directory (packs, fixtures, transformers/manifests/seeds, validator test cases, leakage-detector code and its per-pair overlap scores, planted-leak control case, and the audit-manifest store) before these two gates can be scored true. Until that evidence exists and is embedded/readable, both gates must remain false and no llm_learnability scored trial should begin.
